missions.title: Preference policy
missions.objective: Fit a small categorical policy from comparisons, compare with the reference and inspect held-out preference accuracy.
protocol: Download and extract the workspace. Read README.md and candidate.py; predict the baseline before editing.

python3 -m py_compile candidate.py harness.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s . -p 'test*.py'
python3 harness.py --track posttrain --seed 17 --output posttrain-17.json
Use development runs for tuning. Freeze the candidate hash, then repeat with seeds 113, 271 and 811. Do not keep tuning against those results.
Change preference noise and beta separately; report accuracy and divergence, including a setting that fails.
deliverables: Candidate source, harness and exact invocation
JSON reports with source hash, runtime and metrics
One plot with per-seed points, baseline and ablation; 1-page failure analysis
evaluation: The harness checks a small controlled problem. Inspect each failed check; keep failed runs.
Report mean and spread, never only the best seed. Import the JSON to record evidence; independent review is still required.
A fixed seed set is reproducible, not a secret test set. Ask a peer to choose fresh seeds and altered conditions.

missions.title: Tiny transformer → SFT → preferences
missions.objective: Train a roughly 1–10M parameter decoder on generated arithmetic. Establish SFT, then compare DPO and a verifiable-reward policy update.
protocol: First reproduce your scalar MLP gradients with PyTorch autograd; assert gradient parity and tensor shapes, overfit 32 examples, and test train/eval mode and checkpoint round trips. Then translate the attention and masked-loss drills into tensor operations.
Create a pinned Python/PyTorch environment; record pip freeze, git SHA, accelerator and all config files. Begin with a 100-batch CPU smoke before any GPU run.
Generate disjoint train/validation/test operand tuples. Hold out carry patterns and longer digit lengths; do not split duplicate strings at random.
Implement causal masking, token shift and loss masking. Overfit 32 examples first; compare sampled outputs against exact arithmetic.
Freeze SFT checkpoint. Generate preference pairs only from training prompts. Run DPO and a TRL GRPO baseline with equal sampled-token budgets; report effective KL, reward and response length.
deliverables: Training entrypoint and evaluator, checkpoint, dataset generator and locked split hashes
Loss and held-out exact-match curves; SFT/DPO/GRPO comparison at equal compute
At least three seed runs, reward parsing tests and a reward-hacking example
evaluation: Reject leakage, incorrect masking or train-only improvements. Derive one objective and verify its gradient numerically.
A peer reruns the baseline and one improvement from a clean environment; record differences.
Toy arithmetic is a bridge to post-training research, not evidence of capability on general language tasks.

missions.title: PPO from scratch in a real simulator
missions.objective: Implement PPO with batched environments, GAE, clipped policy loss, value loss and entropy; reproduce a known small-control baseline.
protocol: Translate the scalar MLP into PyTorch tensors and autograd, verify gradient parity, and fit synthetic observations before introducing a changing policy distribution.
Use a version-pinned Gymnasium CartPole then a continuous-control environment. Record wrappers, truncation semantics and observation normalization.
Implement rollout buffer and update loop without copying trainer internals. Compare each tensor on a fixed rollout against an independent implementation.
Run 5 training seeds and at least 20 evaluation episodes per seed. Compare random, reference PPO and your PPO at equal environment-step budgets.
Ablate advantage normalization and clipping independently. Plot learning curves with seed-level uncertainty, not episode samples treated as independent training runs.
deliverables: Runnable trainer, resume checkpoint and fixed-rollout tests
Raw trajectories, configs, 5-seed comparison and two ablations
Diagnosis of one unstable run with hypothesis and counter-experiment
evaluation: Test terminal vs truncated bootstrap, stale log-probs and minibatch shuffling.
Before declaring reproduction define an acceptance interval from the baseline distribution and compute budget.
Peer changes horizon or reward scale during a 90-minute debug session.

missions.title: Attention performance with a cost model
missions.objective: Derive attention memory and FLOPs; reproduce a dense attention baseline and optimize one measured bottleneck.
protocol: Implement causal attention in PyTorch and test outputs/gradients against torch scaled_dot_product_attention for masks, dtypes and awkward shapes.
Write a predicted bytes/FLOPs table for prefill and decode. Benchmark warm runs, synchronize the accelerator and record peak allocated memory, batch, sequence, dtype and device.
Profile before optimizing. Implement one tiled Triton or Pallas kernel only after a correct reference; retain a CPU correctness path.
Sweep shapes and compare median/p95 latency, peak memory and error. Explain where your implementation loses; do not compare different hardware or math modes.
deliverables: Reproducible benchmark CLI and shape matrix with raw measurements
Profiler trace and predicted-vs-observed bottleneck analysis
Correctness/gradient tests and one scoped optimization
evaluation: Correctness is a gate before speed. Use independent repeated processes and report spread.
GPU speed claims require actual GPU runs. Oracle CPU is for smoke/reliability work.
Peer reruns on a clean device and checks an unreported shape.

missions.title: Imitation in a visual simulator
missions.objective: Reproduce a LeRobot policy on a supported simulated task; evaluate trajectories rather than only prediction loss.
protocol: First fit the point-controller dataset with a PyTorch MLP, check tensor shapes and held-out episodes, and verify CPU checkpoint reload parity before introducing pixels and simulator dependencies.
Pin LeRobot and simulator versions. Start from a documented environment configuration and a fixed public dataset version; record camera, action units and control frequency.
Split by complete episode and scene, never adjacent frames. Train a small behavior cloning baseline, then a supported ACT or diffusion policy on the same demonstration budget.
Evaluate at least 50 episodes across seeds and unseen start/goal conditions. Track success, return, collisions, latency and action saturation.
Ablate action chunk length or observation history; add camera noise, latency and dynamics shifts separately. Save videos for successes and failures.
deliverables: Data card and episode split manifest; training/evaluation configs
Checkpoints, evaluation videos, per-episode metrics and latency histogram
Failure taxonomy and paired baseline comparison
evaluation: Low validation action loss is insufficient: require closed-loop evaluation on held-out episodes.
Declare simulator version and unsupported transfer claims; real hardware needs safety constraints and supervised rollout.
Peer changes an unseen scene or disturbance and reviews policy behavior.

missions.title: Audit the reward and data pipeline
missions.objective: Find and fix one real reward, masking or sampling failure in a pinned TRL/verl experiment.
protocol: Inject a malformed answer, zero-variance reward batch and overlong response; write failing tests.
Trace data lineage and compare the fixed run with an unchanged checkpoint on a reserved evaluation set.

Baseline/fix raw measurements and 2-page incident or experiment report
evaluation: Freeze acceptance criteria before the fix. Preserve unsuccessful interventions.
Peer introduces one unrehearsed variant and asks you to diagnose it in 90 minutes.

missions.title: A useful upstream contribution
missions.objective: Choose one active issue in TRL or verl; produce a narrow correction, reproduction or measured improvement another practitioner can use.
protocol: Read current contribution guidance and select a scoped issue that maintainers consider useful. Record the upstream commit and issue URL.
Write a design note: baseline, hypothesis, compute cap, failure cases, acceptance test and cheapest falsifying experiment.
Build the smallest patch with tests and exact reproduction commands. Run a clean-environment replication before opening the PR.
Respond to technical review; publish the raw evidence and what did not work. A private-work equivalent needs an independent internal reviewer and reproducible artifact.
deliverables: Public PR or reviewed private artifact with code and evidence
Independent reproduction log; response to review
10-minute explanation plus 45-minute probing Q&A without AI
evaluation: A merged PR is useful adoption evidence, not a universal qualification. Judge scope, correctness and ownership.
Research readiness additionally requires an original, well-controlled finding and an independent reviewer who can challenge it.
If results are null, document the informative negative result honestly.
